The Police Sub-Inspector of Sanjay Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused
for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 323, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code.
2. Prosecution Cas

e: The marriage of CW1 Smt. Uma and accused was solemnized on 27-09- 2009 at Venkateshwara Swamy Temple at Rajajinagara and thereafter they were residing at No.198, behind Kuvempu School, Nagashettihalli within the limits of Sanjaynagara PS.

After two years,
KABC030842422018 CC No.30837/2018 accused started ill-treating CW1 and subjected her to mental and physical cruelty.

On 03-07-2018 at about 10.00 p.m., the accused picked up quarrel with her, abused her in filthiest language, beaten her and threatened her with criminal intimidation and had taken 8 years old daughter with him thereby committed the alleged offences.
3. First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1 namely Smt. Uma, the PSI of Sanjaynagara police CW8 Sri K. R. Mestrinayak registered a Crime No.137/2018 against the accused for the offenses punishable under Section 498(A), 323, 504 and 506 of IPC, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.
4. Investigation: the PSI of Sanjaynagara police CW8 Sri K. R. Mestrinayak registered FIR against accused and recorded the requisite witnesses and collected the documents.

After completion of investigation, the IO/CW8 has submitted the chargesheet against accused for the offenses punishable under Section 498(A), 323, 504 and 506 of IPC,.
5.
The accused was enlarged on bail at the pre- summoning stage by the order dated 23-07-2018.
Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.

7. Charge: After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A), 323, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
8. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 8 witnesses however examined one witness and exhibited 3 documents.

The learned Sr.APP prayed for issuance of summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served, since the material witness has not supported the case and hence the prosecution side was taken as closed on 23-09-2024.

9. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Uma vs Venkatesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144724841/
2 Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

11. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 27-09-2009 the accused married CW1 Smt.Uma at Venkateshwara Swamy Temple, Rajajinagara and thereafter they were residing at Nagashettyhally, Behind Kuvempu School, No.198, within the limits of Sanjaynagara PS,
at that time the accused picked up quarrel and subjected her to both physically and mentally cruelty thereby resulted in commission of the offence punishable under Sec.498(A) of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that at about said place on 03-07-2018 at 10.00 p.m. accused abused CW1 in filthy KABC030842422018 CC No.30837/2018 language knowingly such insult will provoke breach of peace thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec. 504 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused voluntarily beaten CW1 with hands, kicked with legs and caused hurt thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.323 of IPC?

4. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused threatened CW1 with dire consequences thus committed criminal intimidation thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.506 of IPC?
5. What order?

My findings on the above points are as under:
 Point No.1-4 : In the Negative  Point No.5 : As per final order  REASONS 13. Point No.1 to 4: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 11 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined one witness, which is as follows i. CW1 by name Smt.Uma,
being Informant examined as PW1 deposed that she has identified her signatures on Ex.P1 (complaint) and Ex.P2 (spot mahazar).

She further stated that when she went to police station for Uma vs Venkatesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144724841/
3 settlement of minor grievances between her and accused, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and 2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this regard, the learned Sr.APP has cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her mouth to KABC030842422018 CC No.30837/2018 support the prosecution case.

Her denial of statement given before the police is marked as Ex.P3.
14.
PW1 is the informant cum victim has not supported the prosecution case.
Though the prosecution has cross examined her by treating as hostile witness, no favorable evidence from her mouth to support the prosecution case and she has deposed falsely to help the accused.
15. It is seen from the deposition of PW1 that the disputes between the accused and the PW1 have been settled.

But the learned APP argued that the Section 498A R/w Section 34 of Indian Penal code is not compoundable case as per section 320 of CRPC and hence the examination of witnesses is necessary but this court dispensed the same on account of amicable settlement arrived between the rival parties to the case.
Yes this court agrees with the view of the Learned Sr.APP that the section 498A of IPC is not compoundable and the same cannot be compounded as per Section 320 of CRPC.

This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR IN THE MATTER OF AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then KABC030842422018 CC No.30837/2018 in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
16. This court further places reliance upon the decision in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat), wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances,
KABC030842422018 CC No.30837/2018 under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
17.
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498A of I.P.C. is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/Pw1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

Uma vs Venkatesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144724841/
4 18.

In the matter of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".
19.

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the KABC030842422018 CC No.30837/2018 prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
In this background, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the offence under section 498A of IPC with other offences under section 323, 504, 506 of IPC cannot be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answers the point No.1 to 4 in the Negative.

20. Point No.5:- In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 4, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A), 323, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code.
(ii) Accused is set at liberty.
KABC030842422018 CC No.30837/2018
( iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six) months.
(iv) Ordered accordingly.
